climate_pressure: Rising heat, changing rainfall, drought/flood episodes.
documented_impact: Reduced or disrupted agricultural production and climate-sensitive livelihood stress.
fcv_mediator: Existing land disputes, unequal access, weak resource governance and lack of alternative livelihoods.
possible_consequence: Livelihood pressure may intensify existing disputes or grievances over land and water in parts of eastern DRC.
alternative_explanations: demographic pressure and market conditions independently generate conflict
uncertainty: SIPRI explicitly states that specific livelihood-to-conflict mechanisms remain less clear than the climate-to-livelihood link. (SIPRI2)
resilience_factors: extension services and inclusive resource planning
compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood stress may increase pressure on already contested land and water, but political and governance conditions determine whether tension escalates.

climate_pressure: Recurring drought, rainfall variability and declining pasture/water availability.
documented_impact: Altered livestock mobility and competition for water/pasture.
fcv_mediator: Pre-existing farmer-pastoralist disputes, identity conflict and land-access arrangements.
possible_consequence: Greater tension, livestock theft or violence has been reported locally where altered movement intersects with existing disputes.
uncertainty: Local, largely qualitative evidence; it must not be generalized across South Kivu or nationally.
resilience_factors: participatory land/water governance and agro-pastoral cooperation
compact_statement: In the Ruzizi Plain, climate-sensitive changes in pasture and livestock movement appear to interact with - not originate independently from - existing farmer-pastoralist conflict.

climate_pressure: Extreme rainfall, floods and rainfall-triggered landslides.
fcv_mediator: Overcrowded sites, inadequate basic services, resource scarcity and weak post-disaster recovery.
possible_consequence: Displacement may create or intensify localized tensions between displaced and host communities where services/resources are already scarce.
alternative_explanations: Conflict displacement is far larger in many eastern areas and may independently overwhelm services
poor planning and infrastructure condition flood losses
uncertainty: Disaster-displacement figures should not automatically be interpreted as anthropogenic-climate displacement.
compact_statement: Flood displacement can add pressure to fragile local service/resource systems, potentially worsening grievances where recovery is weak.

climate_pressure: Future drought, flood, heat or rainfall shocks.
documented_impact: Households require access to farmland, markets, services and humanitarian support to cope.
fcv_mediator: Armed-group control, insecurity, road blockage, displacement and restricted territorial access.
possible_consequence: Communities exposed to conflict may experience greater livelihood loss, food insecurity and slower recovery when climate shocks occur.
geographies: North/South Kivu and other conflict-affected eastern provinces
institutions: local authorities and armed actors controlling access
alternative_explanations: infrastructure deficits and commodity-price shocks can also reduce coping capacity outside active conflict
uncertainty: Effects on quantified adaptation outcomes have rarely been evaluated.
resilience_factors: conflict-sensitive adaptation and locally trusted delivery channels
compact_statement: Insecurity can convert otherwise manageable climate shocks into deeper crises by removing access to land, markets, services and recovery assistance. (SIPRI2)

climate_pressure: Climate mitigation/adaptation requires functioning forest, land and ecosystem governance.
documented_impact: Armed actors and political-economic networks exploit forests/minerals and damage environmental governance.
fcv_mediator: Conflict financing, corruption, weak state authority and elite competition.
possible_consequence: Forest-management and resilience objectives may be harder to implement, increasing environmental vulnerability and weakening mitigation capacity.
alternative_explanations: regulatory design and global commodity demand also drive environmental loss
uncertainty: Environmental degradation should not be relabelled as climate damage; specific climate consequences require separate evidence.
resilience_factors: forest monitoring and conflict-sensitive natural-resource governance
compact_statement: FCV-linked extraction can undermine institutions needed for climate mitigation and adaptation, while remaining an independent environmental and political-economy driver. (NUPI3)

documented_impact: Damage to roads, water, electricity, housing and agricultural assets.
fcv_mediator: Poverty, informal settlement, weak drainage/DRM capacity, fiscal limitations and weak coordination.
possible_consequence: Repeated losses could deepen service deficits, recovery burdens and public grievances; violence is not demonstrated by the evidence reviewed.
uncertainty: No source reviewed demonstrates that urban floods cause violence or conflict.
compact_statement: Flood losses place additional pressure on weak urban service systems, but any transition from service stress to FCV outcomes remains unproven. (World Bank5)

climate_pressure: Multi-hazard climate exposure requiring sustained adaptation investment.
documented_impact: Large planned adaptation requirements and implementation needs.
fcv_mediator: Fiscal pressure, weak coordination, governance limitations and - where relevant - conflict-related access constraints.
possible_consequence: Delayed, incomplete or unsustained adaptation may leave households and infrastructure exposed to future shocks.
alternative_explanations: COVID-19 and maintenance failures independently affect performance
uncertainty: National adaptation effectiveness has not been comprehensively evaluated.
resilience_factors: predictable financing and locally owned implementation
compact_statement: Policy ambition exceeds demonstrated delivery capacity, leaving a gap between adaptation plans and sustained resilience outcomes. (IMF7)

documented_impact: Communities face livelihood, displacement and resource-management challenges.
fcv_mediator: Social cohesion, inclusion, local legitimacy and collective action.
possible_consequence: Well-supported women-, youth- and community-led initiatives could reduce vulnerability and strengthen peaceful problem-solving, although programme-level effects on violence are not established.
alternative_explanations: Community organizations may have limited resources
uncertainty: No reviewed evaluation measures whether these initiatives reduce conflict incidence.
resilience_factors: agro-pastoral cooperatives and inclusive customary/local governance
compact_statement: Local social institutions provide credible resilience and peace-supporting capacity, but their impact has not been rigorously quantified. (SIPRI2)
